distinguishing_features: Sacrificial compliant polyurethane layer applied to superheater tubes to absorb slag-impact stress peaks
Geometry of the compliant layer channels slag away from tubes and localizes wear to a renewable element
Passive installation on the lower 20% of tubes with a 15-degree taper
Validation by pressure-spike amplitude reduction during slag-shedding events
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to protect superheater tubes from slag-shedding impact and erosion at high temperature without relying solely on hardening the tube material
parsed.viable_reason: At the stated 400°C superheater operating temperature, polyurethane would degrade and lose adhesion, making the claimed compliant lining physically implausible as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the cited prior art discloses or suggests a sacrificial compliant polymer layer shaped to absorb slag impact and channel slag away from tubes, and it is not a routine parameter change to those references.
